findings.reason: the declared change to a shared helper silently moves the delivery/still-working verdict for the watcher, and a node that implements only what s12 names ships that shift with no gate covering it.
findings.text: s12 states "One reader reads the declared paths rather than the store: `_review_store_record_paths`", but that helper has a second consumer in the same module — `_delivered_review_record` (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py:124`, calling the helper at `:139`), whose only caller `review_delivered` is read by `_stop_delivered_reviews` (`:190,208`) to SIGTERM a review run whose stream outlives its delivery by the grace; broadening the helper to also select run-directory paths (which the deliverable requires) makes a record sitting unfiled in the review run's own directory count as delivered, so the run can be stopped by grace on evidence the plan never names

findings.reason: the done-when's third case already requires `_review_subject` to return its reviewed run and head with a red control, so a builder that picks another leaf name is caught by the node's own gate rather than shipping.
findings.text: s12 explains the run-directory reader gap as "it must learn the run-directory location too. Otherwise the head comes back empty", but `_review_record_subject` (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:130`) recovers both the reviewed run and the head from the record's *filename* (`<run>.json`, `<run>.at-<head>.json`), so the run-directory record must keep that leaf spelling; a run-directory record named otherwise yields a standing-less run id, not merely an empty head, and the deliverable never states the spelling the new location must carry

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited target resolves: `recovery_review_subject.py:610,613` (the two `review.review_path` declarations), `_review_store_record_paths` at `recovery_review_delivery.py:47`, `_review_subject` at `recovery_review_dispatch.py:150`, `_review_head_covers` at `:180`, `_fence_write_roots` at `dispatch_admission.py:1842`, `delivery_write_roots` at `_backends.py:140`, `_supervisor_exit_record` at `dispatch_launch.py:2371`, `python -m reckon.crew.supervisor_main` at `dispatch_launch.py:1869`, `complete` at `promotion.py:143`, and the comment `c-s10-review-store-gap` at the plan's own line 2024.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each of s12's three cases names a declared negative control (widen the grant back to the parent directory, remove the fallback filing, leave `_review_store_record_paths` selecting store paths only), and the first case fails on unfixed code because an absent declared record file still grants its parent, the whole project store directory.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — s12's gate logs go "under the run directory", which is durable, and the incident evidence it cites lives in committed review comments and `docs/state`, never a session scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the section carries section numbering and mechanism prose only; no plan label, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol or a comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — s12's root cause, its `_fence_write_roots`/`_declared_write_grant` mechanism and its supervisor-outside-the-fence claim all match the code, but its reader inventory is wrong: `_review_store_record_paths` has two consumers, not the one the deliverable names, and the second one's verdict changes under the instructed fix.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s12 carries one deliverable, that a run review's fence grants nothing writable holding another run's record; the run-directory delivery, the supervisor filing and the reader adjustment are the one chosen shape, not separate goals.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s12 declares no section-level links, as every other section of this plan does, and the relationship it relies on (the §10 seal it repairs) is already landed, so nothing it needs is missing.
